definition: Collective experience is the shared psychological experience of a group or humanity as people face common conditions or events. In this source, it especially refers to how cultural narratives help people understand and organize shared responses to environmental change and related collective trauma.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence is broader than the packet: the packet does not describe “the shared psychological experience of a group or humanity as people face common conditions or events” in general terms; it instead discusses a specific mechanism (narrative traditions) and a specific target of meaning (human-nature relations, boundary cognition, and environmental/earth-system changes).

The definition’s claim that it “especially refers to” cultural narratives helping people “understand and organize shared responses” to “environmental change” and “related collective trauma” is only partially supported: the packet says narratives provide a cultural-psychological form for understanding/sorting out/explaining “the collective experience” of dealing with “changes of the earth’s system” and “related human collective trauma,” but it does not explicitly frame this as organizing “shared responses.”
